constructions.label: N + くらいです: about the only one
N + くらいしか + negative: hardly anything but N
言える: the text supports the claim
言えない: the text does not establish the claim
Noun + のあまり: so much that (cause of a result)
あまりの + noun: an extreme degree as the cause
Noun + ばかり: mostly, nothing but
Dictionary form + ばかりだ: keeps changing one way
た-form + ばかり: has only just happened
〜は言うまでもない: goes without saying (predicate)
言うまでもなく: needless to say (connective)
A はもちろん B も: A of course, and B too
A をはじめ(とする) B: A as the leading example of B
A ばかりでなく B も: not only A but also B
A だけでなく B も: not only A but also B
A ばかりで、B: just A, and B is lacking

relationships.label: About the only one: くらい before です versus くらいしか before a negative
Read degree and addition expressions without over-reading them
Excess: choose のあまり, あまりの or あまりに by the slot
Limit: ばかり (mostly) versus だけ (exactly) and しか (with a negative)
Before ばかり: dictionary form for a continuing trend, た-form for a recent event
Goes without saying: predicate 言うまでもない versus connective 言うまでもなく
Adding to an obvious case (はもちろん) versus naming a leading example (をはじめ)
Addition (ばかりでなく／だけでなく) versus just A with a shortcoming (ばかりで)

exercises.prompt: 夜十時を過ぎると、この町の店はほとんど開いていないので、買い物ができるのは駅前のコンビニ____だ。
exercises.translation: Insert only くらい or くらいしか. ぐらい／ぐらいしか and the kanji spelling 位 are also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank is governed by the final affirmative だ; the negative 開いていない belongs to the earlier ので clause.
exercises.explanation: After ten at night hardly any shops in this town are open, so about the only place you can shop is the convenience store in front of the station. In 〜のは N くらいだ, くらい presents N as about the only member of the topic set.

options.label: くらい
options.rationale: Fits: 〜のは N くらいだ means 'about the only one is N'; the blank is governed by affirmative だ, not by the earlier 開いていない. ぐらい and 位 are accepted spellings.

options.label: くらいしか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: くらいしか needs a following negative predicate, but the blank is followed by affirmative だ; the negative 開いていない belongs to the earlier ので clause.

spans.gloss: area in front of the station

exercises.prompt: この町には、夜遅くまで開いている店が、もう駅前のコンビニ____残っていない。
exercises.translation: Insert only くらい or くらいしか. ぐらい／ぐらいしか and the kanji spelling 位 are also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank is followed by the negative verb 残っていない.
exercises.explanation: In this town, apart from the convenience store in front of the station, there are hardly any shops left that stay open late at night. N くらいしか + negative limits the set to roughly N alone.

options.label: くらい
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: without しか, くらい before the negative 残っていない does not give 'about the only one'; with a negative predicate the limiting reading needs くらいしか.

options.label: くらいしか
options.rationale: Fits: くらいしか with the negative 残っていない says that, roughly, N is the only one left.

spans.gloss: area in front of the station

exercises.prompt: 料理は苦手なので、私が作れるのはカレー____です。
exercises.translation: Insert only くらい or くらいしか. ぐらい／ぐらいしか and the kanji spelling 位 are also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank follows the noun in a 〜のは … です sentence; the predicate is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: I'm not good at cooking, so about the only thing I can make is curry. 〜のは N くらいです names N as about the only item and sounds modest.

options.label: くらい
options.rationale: Fits: 〜のは N くらいです means 'about the only one is N'. ぐらい and 位 are accepted spellings.

options.label: くらいしか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: くらいしか needs a following negative predicate (…しかありません), but here the blank is followed by affirmative です.

exercises.prompt: 料理は苦手なので、作れるものはカレー____ありません。
exercises.translation: Insert only くらい or くらいしか. ぐらい／ぐらいしか and the kanji spelling 位 are also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank is followed by the negative predicate ありません.
exercises.explanation: I'm not good at cooking, so there's hardly anything I can make apart from curry. N くらいしか + negative says that, roughly, nothing but N is available.

options.label: くらい
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: without しか, くらい before the negative ありません does not give 'about the only one'; with a negative predicate the limiting reading needs くらいしか.

options.label: くらいしか
options.rationale: Fits: くらいしか with the negative ありません says curry is about the only dish I can make.

exercises.prompt: 日本語の勉強を始めたころは、新聞でわかったのは天気予報____でした。
exercises.translation: Insert only くらい or くらいしか. ぐらい／ぐらいしか and the kanji spelling 位 are also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank follows the noun in a 〜のは … でした sentence; the predicate is affirmative (past).
exercises.explanation: When I had just started studying Japanese, about the only thing I could understand in the newspaper was the weather forecast.

options.label: くらい
options.rationale: Fits: 〜のは N くらいでした means 'about the only one was N'. ぐらい and 位 are accepted spellings.

options.label: くらいしか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: くらいしか needs a following negative predicate (…しかありません), but here the blank is followed by affirmative でした.

exercises.prompt:
文章：このあたりで夜遅くまで開いている店は、駅前のコンビニくらいです。
主張：このあたりには、夜遅くまで開いている店がほとんどない。
____
exercises.translation: From the Japanese text alone, judge the claim: 言える（いえる, supported） or 言えない（いえない, not established）. An unestablished claim need not be false.
exercises.evidence: N くらいです presents N as about the only shop, so shops open late are scarce.
exercises.explanation: Text: Around here, about the only shop open late at night is the convenience store in front of the station. Claim: Around here, there are hardly any shops open late at night. N くらいです presents N as about the only member of the set, which supports 'hardly any'.

options.label: 言える
options.rationale: Text: Around here, about the only shop open late at night is the convenience store in front of the station. Claim: Around here, there are hardly any shops open late at night. N くらいです presents N as about the only member of the set, which supports 'hardly any'.

options.label: 言えない
options.rationale: The claim is supported here. N くらいです presents N as about the only member of the set, which supports 'hardly any'.

spans.gloss: area in front of the station

exercises.prompt:
文章：私が作れる料理は、カレーくらいです。
主張：私はカレーを作るのがとても上手だ。
____
exercises.translation: From the Japanese text alone, judge the claim: 言える（いえる, supported） or 言えない（いえない, not established）. An unestablished claim need not be false.
exercises.evidence: くらいです limits the set of dishes; it says nothing about skill.
exercises.explanation: Text: About the only dish I can make is curry. Claim: I am very good at making curry. N くらいです says curry is about the only dish I can make. It gives no information about skill, and the modest framing points to a small repertoire rather than expertise.

options.label: 言える
options.rationale: The text does not establish this claim. N くらいです says curry is about the only dish I can make. It gives no information about skill, and the modest framing points to a small repertoire rather than expertise.

options.label: 言えない
options.rationale: Text: About the only dish I can make is curry. Claim: I am very good at making curry. N くらいです says curry is about the only dish I can make. It gives no information about skill, and the modest framing points to a small repertoire rather than expertise.

exercises.prompt:
文章：今日はたくさん歩いて、足が痛くて、もう一歩も歩けないくらいです。
主張：話している人の足は、とても痛い。
____
exercises.translation: From the Japanese text alone, judge the claim: 言える（いえる, supported） or 言えない（いえない, not established）. An unestablished claim need not be false.
exercises.evidence: Sentence-final 〜くらいです measures how strong the pain is by an extreme comparison.
exercises.explanation: Text: I walked a lot today, and my feet hurt so much I feel I can't take another step. Claim: The speaker's feet hurt a lot. Sentence-final 〜くらいです measures the degree of the preceding state (the pain) by an extreme comparison, so strong pain is stated.

options.label: 言える
options.rationale: Text: I walked a lot today, and my feet hurt so much I feel I can't take another step. Claim: The speaker's feet hurt a lot. Sentence-final 〜くらいです measures the degree of the preceding state (the pain) by an extreme comparison, so strong pain is stated.

options.label: 言えない
options.rationale: The claim is supported here. Sentence-final 〜くらいです measures the degree of the preceding state (the pain) by an extreme comparison, so strong pain is stated.

exercises.prompt:
文章：昨日見た映画は悲しくて、泣きたいくらいでした。
主張：話している人は、映画を見て泣いた。
____
exercises.translation: From the Japanese text alone, judge the claim: 言える（いえる, supported） or 言えない（いえない, not established）. An unestablished claim need not be false.
exercises.evidence: 泣きたいくらい measures the sadness by a wish to cry; it does not report crying.
exercises.explanation: Text: The film I saw yesterday was so sad that I felt like crying. Claim: The speaker cried while watching the film. 泣きたいくらいでした measures how sad the film was by the wish to cry. It does not state that the speaker actually cried.

options.label: 言える
options.rationale: The text does not establish this claim. 泣きたいくらいでした measures how sad the film was by the wish to cry. It does not state that the speaker actually cried.

options.label: 言えない
options.rationale: Text: The film I saw yesterday was so sad that I felt like crying. Claim: The speaker cried while watching the film. 泣きたいくらいでした measures how sad the film was by the wish to cry. It does not state that the speaker actually cried.

exercises.prompt: 試験に合格したと聞いて、母はうれしさ____泣き出した。
exercises.translation: Insert only のあまり, あまりの or あまりに. The kanji spelling 余り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The blank follows the emotion noun うれしさ and precedes the result it caused.
exercises.explanation: When she heard I had passed the exam, my mother was so happy that she burst into tears. Noun + のあまり says a feeling or state was so strong that it caused the result that follows.

options.label: のあまり
options.rationale: Fits: after the noun うれしさ, のあまり links the feeling to the result it caused.

options.label: あまりの
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: あまりの must come before a noun (あまりのうれしさに…); here it would follow うれしさ and run straight into a verb clause.

options.label: あまりに
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: あまりに modifies a following adjective or adverb; it cannot attach directly after the noun うれしさ.

exercises.prompt: ____暑さに、昼間は外を歩いている人がほとんどいない。

exercises.evidence: The blank opens the sentence directly before the さ-noun 暑さ.
exercises.explanation: The heat is so extreme that hardly anyone is walking outside in the daytime. あまりの + noun (often a さ-noun) + に presents an extreme degree as the cause of what follows.

options.label: のあまり
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: のあまり must follow a noun (…のあまり); here the blank stands before the noun 暑さ, so a noun-modifying form is needed.

options.label: あまりの
options.rationale: Fits: あまりの modifies 暑さ and, with に, gives the extreme degree as the cause.

options.label: あまりに
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: あまりに modifies an adjective or adverb; before the noun 暑さ the attributive あまりの is needed.

exercises.prompt: 今日のテストは____難しくて、だれも最後の問題に答えられなかった。

exercises.evidence: The blank stands before the adjective 難しくて.
exercises.explanation: Today's test was so difficult that nobody could answer the last question. あまりに (also あまりにも, あんまりに, あんまりにも, あんまり) raises an adjective or adverb to an excessive degree, usually followed by its result.

options.label: のあまり
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: のあまり follows a noun; here the blank stands before the adjective 難しくて and there is no noun for it to attach to.

options.label: あまりの
options.rationale: Does not fit this slot: あまりの modifies a noun; before the adjective 難しくて the adverbial あまりに is needed.

options.label: あまりに
options.rationale: Fits: あまりに modifies the adjective 難しくて and marks the degree as excessive.

exercises.explanation: Today it is so hot that hardly anyone is walking outside in the daytime. あまりに (also あまりにも, あんまりに, あんまりにも, あんまり) raises an adjective or adverb to an excessive degree, usually followed by its result.

options.label: のあまり

exercises.prompt: 野菜も少しは食べますが、息子は肉____食べています。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The first clause admits a few exceptions, and the predicate is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: My son eats a few vegetables too, but he eats mostly meat. Noun + ばかり says one kind of thing dominates (often with a critical tone) while tolerating a few exceptions.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Fits: ばかり says meat dominates his diet, which allows the few vegetables mentioned first.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: だけ would make meat literally the only food, which the first clause (he eats some vegetables) contradicts.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: しか needs a negative predicate, but 食べています is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: 友だちも二人いましたが、パーティーは知らない人____で、少し緊張しました。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: Two friends were present, so the rest is a large majority, not a complete set; the sentence is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: Two of my friends were there too, but the party was mostly people I didn't know, so I felt a little nervous. Noun + ばかりで describes a crowd dominated by one kind of member.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Fits: ばかり says strangers made up most of the party, which allows the two friends.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: だけ would say everyone there was a stranger, which contradicts the two friends.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: しか needs a negative predicate, but …で、緊張しました is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: 女の子も三人いますが、このクラスは男の子____です。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: Three girls are present, so boys are a large majority, not the whole class; the predicate is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: There are three girls as well, but this class is mostly boys.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Fits: ばかり says boys dominate the class, which allows the three girls.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: だけ would say the class is boys only, which contradicts the three girls.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: しか needs a negative predicate, but です is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: このクーポンが使えるのは、一人一回____です。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The sentence states an exact rule limit, and the predicate is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: This coupon can be used only once per person. だけ states an exact limit.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: after a number, ばかり reads as 'about', which does not suit an exact usage rule, and its 'mostly' sense does not apply to a count.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Fits: だけ states the exact limit: one use per person and no more.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: しか needs a negative predicate, but です is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: 昨日の会議に出たのは、部長と私の二人____でした。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: Two named people form an exact, complete set, and the predicate is affirmative.
exercises.explanation: Only two people attended yesterday's meeting: the manager and me.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: after a number, ばかり reads as 'about', which does not suit two named people.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Fits: だけ gives the exact, complete set of attendees.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Does not fit this sentence: しか needs a negative predicate, but でした is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: 息子は好き嫌いが多くて、肉____食べません。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかり, だけ or しか. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The predicate is negative, and a fussy eater rejects most foods.
exercises.explanation: My son is a fussy eater and won't eat anything but meat. しか + negative says nothing other than N.

options.label: ばかり
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: 肉ばかり食べません would only deny that he eats mostly meat, which does not follow from being a fussy eater.

options.label: だけ
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: 肉だけ食べません would make meat the one food he refuses, which does not match a child with many dislikes.

options.label: しか
options.rationale: Fits: しか with the negative 食べません says meat is the only thing he eats.

exercises.prompt: 財布を開けたら、百円____入っていなかった。

exercises.evidence: The predicate is negative, and the amount is presented as all there was.

exercises.evidence: B is added with も; both are things you can borrow.
exercises.explanation: At this library you can borrow not only books but also film DVDs. A だけでなく B も/でも… adds B to A; B is of the same kind (both good or both bad).

options.label: ばかりで

exercises.explanation: After all that walking, not only do my feet hurt, but my head has started to ache too. A だけでなく B も/でも… adds B to A; B is of the same kind (both good or both bad).

options.label: だけでなく

exercises.explanation: Not only the children but also lots of parents and neighbours came to the sports day. A だけでなく B も/でも… adds B to A; B is of the same kind (both good or both bad).

options.label: ばかりで
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ばかりで would present A as the only feature and lead into a shortcoming, but the next clause adds a further point of the same kind with も.

exercises.prompt: この店の料理は安い____、味はよくない。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかりでなく or ばかりで. Variants such as ばかりではなく are accepted.
exercises.evidence: B is a shortcoming contrasted with は, not a further good point added with も.
exercises.explanation: The food at this restaurant is cheap, and that's all; it doesn't taste good. A ばかりで、B… says A is all there is (often something unimpressive) and B is lacking or goes wrong.

options.label: ばかりでなく
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ばかりでなく adds a further point of the same kind (usually with も), but here the next clause contrasts with は and denies good taste.

exercises.prompt: 今日の会議では、三時間も話し合う____、結局何も決まらなかった。
exercises.translation: Insert only だけでなく or ばかりで. Variants such as だけではなく and だけじゃなく are accepted.
exercises.evidence: A is effort spent (三時間も話し合う), and 結局 reports B as the disappointing result of that effort, the reading that A ばかりで、B expresses.
exercises.explanation: At today's meeting we did nothing but talk for three hours, and in the end nothing was decided. A ばかりで、B… says A is all there is (often something unimpressive) and B is lacking or goes wrong.

options.label: だけでなく
options.rationale: Does not give the natural reading here: だけでなく adds B as a further point in the same direction as A, usually marked with も. This sentence instead reports B (nothing was decided) as the disappointing result of all that talking, which is what A ばかりで、B expresses.

options.label: ばかりで
options.rationale: Fits: 話し合うばかりで says talking was all that happened, and 結局 leads into the lack of any decision.

exercises.prompt: 弟は毎日ゲームをする____、宿題は全然しない。
exercises.translation: Insert only ばかりでなく or ばかりで. Variants such as ばかりではなく are accepted.
exercises.evidence: A is the one activity he does every day, and B, set against it with は, is what goes undone.
exercises.explanation: My younger brother does nothing but play games every day and doesn't do his homework at all. Dictionary form + ばかりで says one activity is all that gets done and leads into what is neglected. A ばかりで、B… says A is all there is (often something unimpressive) and B is lacking or goes wrong.

options.label: ばかりでなく
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ばかりでなく affirms A and adds B alongside it as a further point; here the next clause sets homework against the games with は (games, yes; homework, never), which is the A ばかりで、B pattern.

options.label: ばかりで
options.rationale: Fits: ゲームをするばかりで says playing games is all he does and leads into the homework he never does.

introductionGroups.label: About the only one, and sentence-final くらい for extent

introductionGroups.label: Excess that causes a result: のあまり, あまりの and あまりに

あまりに + adjective/adverb: excessively

introductionGroups.label: ばかり: mostly, keeps changing, or has just happened
